summary:
Plan of w137 is written as far as it goes; three questions remain open.
All four scenarios (r70, r80, r71, r83) fail at their first Given: no step writes a proposal with Questions and Answers. Run.items reads work-items only, workqueue.move refuses approved and formulated, and no round brief or session exists.
Decided:
- r70 applies only to awaiting-answer proposals.
- A round runs as an initiative-round worker through Workers.worker.
- A round 'ends' when it leaves a readable result.
- Apply and formulate run in one work run, each transition committed through Run.move.
- workqueue.move checks statuses by the node's kind; items() is unchanged.
- A new module, scripts/supervise_rounds.py, plus a CLAUDE.md row.
The decisions break no tests.
Open questions: where a round's commits land; an awaiting-answer proposal with no questions; what a faulted round makes of the proposal.
questions: Where do the commits of an apply or formulate round go? The round commits spec/ (apply) or features/ (formulate) in the worktree work run gives it, and no supervision line says what becomes of them. Reading A: work run merges the round's branch into the initiative branch when the round ends, before the proposal's transition; the person sees spec/ and features/ changed on the initiative branch, with p1 approved and then formulated. Reading B: the round's branch is kept unmerged, as r26 keeps a work-item branch; the person sees p1 approved and then formulated, spec/ and features/ unchanged on the initiative branch, and the round's commits on a kept branch.

Does r70 start an apply round for an awaiting-answer capability-proposal that has no question at all? This happens when a gate's result gives none. Reading A: yes, 'every question has an answer' holds, so apply starts given no answers; the person sees p1 approved and then formulated in the same run. Reading B: no, no round starts; the person sees p1 stay awaiting-answer, and work run exits as it does on an awaiting-answer node.

What happens to a capability-proposal whose apply or formulate round's session ends in an error, at its turn limit, or without a readable result? Reading A: work run moves the proposal to failed and writes the fault under its ## Faults, as r45 does for a work-item; the person sees p1 failed, and work run exits with an error naming p1 and its fault. Reading B: the proposal keeps its status and work run exits with an error naming p1's round and its fault; the person sees p1 still awaiting-answer (or approved), and the next work run starts the round again.
